ar_wood_wall.blurb: Wood Wall is a small sport crag in the Rock Creek zone of the Big Piney country, in the Ozarks of north-central Arkansas. It holds 15 bolted lines on sandstone, and the wall is smooth, with big bulges and interesting holds. The grades lean hard: seven of the routes are 5.11, three are 5.12 and one is 5.13, with only a handful of easier lines in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. That makes it a good stop for strong climbers already working the steep, powerful style Rock Creek is known for, and less useful for a day of moderates. Rock Creek's cliff band runs roughly 50 to 80 feet tall, in a quiet, backwoods setting.

ar_roman_wall.blurb: Roman Wall sits on the east side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas, on a long crag that faces west and catches the afternoon sun. Thirteen of its 15 routes are sport and two are trad, on sandstone. The wall is best known for a dense run of 5.10 and 5.11 lines, with four of each, plus a few easier pitches from around 5.4 to 5.9 and a single 5.12. Routes here are among the better ones on the east side of the canyon. The hike from the main valley is long and uphill, so plan for a committing day rather than a quick lap.

ar_foxy_wall.blurb: Foxy Wall is the right-hand section of Ode Hollow, a compact sandstone cliff near the headwaters of Big Piney Creek in north-central Arkansas. All 15 routes are sport, running from 5.10 through 5.14, with five at 5.10, five at 5.11, three at 5.12 and a couple of hard 5.13 and 5.14 lines. The wall is colourful, rock quality is high, and big huecos give the climbing an unusual flavour for the state, with a power-and-technique character. This is not a beginner wall: there are few easy options, so it suits climbers comfortable on 5.10 and up. The walk in to Ode Hollow is long and steep.

ct_fat_man_s_squeeze.blurb: Fat Man's Squeeze is a small bouldering zone along a trail in the Chatfield Hollow area of Killingworth, Connecticut. It is known for steep roofs, overhangs and tight corridors, so the climbing here is more about powerful moves under cover than about slabs. All 15 problems are boulders on gneiss, and the spread is wide: a few easy V1 and V2 problems, a solid middle run through V3 to V6, and two hard V8 lines. Beginners can find a warm-up, but most of the tall-grade lines will suit people who already like steep, strenuous bouldering.

ct_split_boulder_2.blurb: Split Boulder is a secluded cluster in the Hillside Boulders section of Hurd Park in Connecticut, up a hill from the park road. A large boulder stands in front of a high rock face, and the stone is good quality on both. The 15 problems are all bouldering, mostly in the V2 to V4 range with a handful of easier ones and a few harder problems reaching V7. It makes a fine short session for a small group, with enough moderate problems for a mixed-ability party. Expect hornets and yellow jackets around the cracks from spring through autumn.

ct_ball_field_slabs.blurb: Ball Field Slabs is a cliff in West Rock State Park above the town ball fields in New Haven, with views over the city and Long Island Sound. Its 15 routes are mostly multi-pitch, with a mix of trad (eight), sport (six) and a top rope, from about 5.7 to 5.11. Most grades sit between 5.7 and 5.9, and the lines are long and moderate, though several need a 70 m rope. Solid rock is limited, bolts can be sparse, and blocks can come loose, so wear a helmet and treat these as serious routes rather than a typical sport crag.

ct_motocross_valley_dark_tower.blurb: This bouldering zone lies in the far southwest corner of Paugnut State Forest, within the Burr Pond State Park complex in Connecticut. Two large boulders, around 15 to 22 feet tall, carry 15 problems on pink granitic gneiss with black and pink banding. Landings are fairly clear, and there is a safe way down. Most problems are easy to moderate, running from VB through V4 with one V5 above that, with slopers, flakes and friction-heavy holds. It works well as a warm-up before heading deeper into the woods for the pink granite maze, and as an introduction to granite bouldering for climbers coming from the gym.

ct_slabs_and_cave.blurb: Slabs and Cave is a small cliff band with slabs and a little cave inside Mianus Park, on the Greenwich and Stamford border in Connecticut. All 15 problems are bouldering, and they run easy: eight sit at V1, with a V0, a V2, two at V3 and three at V4. The slabs give beginners a friendly place to start, while the cave adds harder, steeper problems. It sits just past the parking lot on the Greenwich side, so it is a convenient short session or a first outdoor boulder day.
